title: Lunceford's band at Casa Manana and Eddie Wilcox's arrangements
summary: Rowles thinks the Lunceford band outplayed everyone and credits Eddie Wilcox with many arrangements.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, I'll be darned. I thought it was a heart attack. Boy, what a band that was. That was some band, wasn't it.
I never got to see them in their prime.
Oh boy, you missed it. There was nobody on earth that could stand up to that band. I don't care, you
take Duke Ellington, you take the whole works, put them all together, and Jimmie Lunceford would blow them out of the place.
They used to have a place out in Culver City in Los Angeles called Casa Manana. And he had an arrangement, I think the piano player wrote it...

Yeah. He wrote an awful lot of arrangements that he didn't get credit for. Sy Oliver is supposed to have written the whole thing. No. Eddie Wilcox wrote an awful lot of that stuff, like "Sleepy Time Gal," you know, with that double time...
That saxophone thing. That's Eddie Wilcox. And "Blues In The Night," that's Eddie Wilcox. A lot of them are Eddie Wilcox. I know Eddie Wilcox. I knew him real well.
